descriptions.text:
This course introduces students to modern Hindi literature through a thematic and analytical approach. It explores key themes in contemporary Hindi writing, including women’s writing and gender discourse; subaltern perspectives (with a focus on Dalit and Adivasi literature); narratives of mobility, partition, and displacement; and representations of ageing. These themes are examined in relation to the broader socio-cultural and political contexts of post-independence India.

Class discussions focus primarily on close reading of literary texts, with attention to textual, narratological, discursive, and stylistic analysis. These analyses are further enriched through engagement with selected secondary and theoretical readings.

Course materials include a range of texts in Hindi, such as short stories, excerpts from novels, poems, and travelogues, alongside relevant critical and theoretical works. The course also provides an introduction to the historical development of Hindi literary traditions.

**Reading List**
Selected literary texts and secondary readings will be made available via Brightspace. Additional materials may be provided in class. The course includes a range of modern Hindi literary texts across genres (short stories, poems, and excerpts from longer works). Texts will be read and critically analysed in class in conjunction with relevant secondary and theoretical readings. Students are expected to familiarize themselves with assigned texts prior to class. The final selection of readings may be adjusted during the course.

### **Primary Sources (Indicative Selection)**

The course draws on works by major authors of modern Hindi and Urdu literature, including: Sūryabālā, Gulzār, Sañjīv, Bhīṣm Sāhnī, Omprakāś Vālmīkī, Yaśpāl, Sudhā Arorā, Alkā Sarāvgī, Jagdambā Prasād Dīkṣit, Sādat Ḥasan Manṭo, Nirmalā Putul, Svayaṃ Prakāś, Premcand, and others.
**Indicative texts include:**

* *Taqsīm* – Gulzār (story; Partition and displacement)
* *Jvār* – Sañjīv (story; Partition and displacement)
* *Nūr Miyā̃* – Rameśaṅkar Yādav ‘Vidrohī’ (poem; Partition)
* *Baujī aur Bandar* – Sūryabālā (story; ageing)
* *Rahogī Tum Vahī* – Sudhā Arorā (story; gender, domesticity, violence)
* *Pacīs Caukā Ḍeṛh Sau* – Omprakāś Vālmīkī (story; Dalit literature)
* *Muhabbat* – Jagdambā Prasād Dīkṣit (story; urban life, marginality)
* *Cīf kī Dāvat* – Bhīṣm Sāhnī (story; ageing)
* *Cauthā Hādsā* – Svayaṃ Prakāś (story; communal relations)
* *Malbe kā Mālik* – Mohan Rākeś (story; aftermath of Partition)
* *Gū̃gā Nahī̃ Thā Main* – Jayprakāś Kardam (poem; Dalit literature)

### **Additional / Optional Readings**

* *Vah Bhī Koī Deś Hai Mahārāj* (excerpt) – Anil Yādav (travel writing; marginal regions)
* *Dājyu* – Śekhar Jośī (story; nostalgia; rural–urban transition)
* *Yahā̃ Kamalinī Khiltī Hai* – Mṛdulā Garg (story; gender discourse)

### **Secondary Readings (Indicative)**

Culler, Jonathan. *Literary Theory: A Very Short Introduction*. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1997.
Gaeffke, Peter. “Hindi Literature in the Twentieth Century.” In *History of Indian Literature*, vol. 8, edited by J. Gonda. Wiesbaden: Otto Harrassowitz, 1978.
Gupta, Dipankar. *Social Stratification*. New Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1992.
Khilnani, Sunil. *The Idea of India*. London: Hamish Hamilton, 1997.
Dube, S. C. *Indian Society*. New Delhi: National Book Trust, 2005.
Uberoi, Patricia. *Freedom and Destiny: Gender, Family, and Popular Culture in India*. New Delhi: Oxford University Press, 2006.

*Note: The reading list may be adapted depending on the focus and progression of the course.*

* Attendance, class preparation and participation: 10% of final grade
* Homework & weekly assignments: 10% of final grade
* A mid-term paper (discussion and critical analysis of a Hindi text prepared at home by student and to be uploaded by Turnitin on BB : 30%
* A final paper (assessment of text and critical analyses prepared at home by student and to be uploaded by Turnitin on BB): 50%
    In order to pass the course, students must obtain an overall mark of “5.50” (=6) or higher.

Enrolment through [MyStudyMap](https://mijn.universiteitleiden.nl/login) is mandatory.General information about course and exam enrolment is available on the [website]( https://www.student.universiteitleiden.nl/en/your-study-programme/courses-and-exams/enrolment/humanities/english-language-and-culture-ba?cf=humanities&cd=english-language-and-culture-ba#tab-2)

Having successfully finished [5482K2HI Hindi 4](https://studiegids.universiteitleiden.nl/courses/127875/hindi-4). Please; contact the student advisor or A. Avtans MA MPhil; if you are interested in taking this course; but do NOT fulfill the above mentioned requirement.

* For substantive questions; contact the lecturer listed in the right information bar.* For questions about enrolment; admission; etc; contact the Education Administration Office [Herta Mohr](https://www.organisatiegids.universiteitleiden.nl/en/faculties-and-institutes/humanities/faculty-office/student-affairs/education-administration-offices/herta-mohr-education-administration-office)

* Seminar (One two hour tutorial every week.)

Attendance and participation are obligatory. Classes missed for a good reason (to the discretion of the conveners and to be discussed BEFORE the class takes place) will have to be made up with an extra assignment. Being absent without notification can result in a lower grade or exclusion from the term end exams and a failing grade for the course.

Being absent will result in a lowering of the In-class performance & participation grade with 0.5 for every absence after the first two (2) times.

#### Resit

If you fail this course, you can resubmit an improved version of your final paper (50% of the final grade). In case of resubmission of this paper (insufficient final grade only). The deadline for resubmission is 10 working days after receiving the grade for the paper.

#### Review and feedback

How and when an exam review will take place will be disclosed together with the publication of the exam results at the latest. If a student requests a review within 30 days after publication of the exam results, an exam review will have to be organized.

descriptions.value: Acquiring knowledge by systematically and methodically inquiring into a situation or concept, making use of methods appropriate to the academic field or discipline.
Kennis verwerven door het systematisch en methodisch bevragen van een situatie of concept waarbij gebruik gemaakt wordt van methoden die passen bij het vakgebied of de discipline.
Analysing situations or information and deciding what is of major and lesser importance. Seeing interrelationships and getting to the core of the matter.
Ontleden van situaties of een hoeveelheid informatie in hoofd- en bijzaken. Zien van onderlinge verbanden en doordringen tot de kern.
Setting out ideas and information clearly in writing, taking account of the relevant target group and in such a way that the message is received and understood.
Ideeën en informatie helder op schrift stellen, rekening houdend met de doelgroep, en zodanig dat de boodschap overkomt en wordt begrepen.
Being well-informed about societal, political and discipline-related developments and being aware of own role and influence within these developments.
Goed geïnformeerd zijn over de maatschappelijke, politieke en vakinhoudelijke ontwikkelingen en zich bewust zijn van de eigen rol en invloed binnen deze ontwikkelingen.

Critically evaluating own and others’ behaviour, viewpoints or methods, and being open to evaluation by others. Being able to learn from these evaluations by changing own behaviour, viewpoints or methods.

Het kritisch evalueren van (eigen) gedrag, standpunten of methoden en open staan voor evaluatie door anderen. Het vermogen om te leren van deze evaluaties door wijziging van het eigen gedrag, standpunten of methoden.
Self-directing own process of absorbing and applying new knowledge and information.
Zelf sturing geven aan het eigen proces van nieuwe kennis en informatie opnemen en toepassen.
